author: ValWood
body:
Cysteine hydrolase whose endogenous substrates and physiological function are unknown. 
 Catalyzes the hydrolytic activation of several ester-based prodrugs, by cleaving the dioxolone ring to yield their respective active metabolites, diacetyl and CO2. Can thus convert the prodrugs Olmesartan medoxomil and Azilsartan medoxomil into their active metabolites (Olmesartan and Azilsartan), two angiotensin receptor blockers. Is also able to activate beta-lactam antibiotics Faropenem medoxomil and Lenampicillin.2 publications

UniProt has only annotated to "hydrolase activity" which seems correct.

but there is a Reactome TAS to GO:0006805  xenobiotic metabolic process
which seems out of scope

author: deustp01
body:
> but there is a Reactome TAS to GO:0006805 xenobiotic metabolic process
> which seems out of scope

Why out of scope? Humans encounter these two small molecules as drugs, which are a (mostly) benign form of xenobiotic. Endogenous enzymes that surely did not evolve to metabolize these foreign molecules, are co-opted to do so. Isn't that what xenobiotic metabolism is? Is there a better GO term for the metabolic processes that humans use to metabolize ingested drugs? (No objection to re-annotating, but it would be good to do it consistently and with terms that will remain valid, over a fairly large number of processes.

author: ValWood
body: Hi @deustp01  yes this seems OK. I was focused on the  physiological function, which is unknown, but it seems clear that this is a detoxification enzyme   for endogenous toxins in higher eukaryotes. I will annotate  to "detoxification" based on this
